name: Permission
tagline: You're here. That's enough for now.
gain: Emotional permission to face reality alongside hope.
description: Name what you hope for. Name what you fear. Give yourselves permission to walk both roads at once — hope and preparation are both acts of love.

exercises.title: Hopes and Fears
exercises.blurb: A map of what you're hoping for and what keeps you up at night — on paper, not just in your head.

exercises.title: Walk Two Roads
exercises.blurb: Your family's shared declaration that hope and preparation are both acts of love.

exercises.title: Good Days / Bad Days
exercises.blurb: A concrete picture of what good and bad days actually look like — for your loved one AND for you.

name: Clarity
tagline: Now you know who you are and what matters.
gain: A clear understanding of yourself, your values, and what matters most — articulated in words that can travel anywhere.
description: Before you can advocate, you have to know what you are advocating for. Replace assumption with articulation.

exercises.title: What Matters to Me
exercises.blurb: One sentence about what matters most — portable enough to hand to any doctor in any country.

exercises.title: Important To / Important For
exercises.blurb: A clear view of the tension between what your loved one wants and what they need.

exercises.title: One Page Profile
exercises.blurb: A single page that introduces your loved one as a person, not just a patient — printable, shareable, translatable.

name: Connection
tagline: You're not doing this alone. Here is your team.
gain: A visible, organized team with named roles, defined responsibilities, and mapped relationships.
description: Name who's in. Identify the caregiver and the backup decision-maker (often different people, often in different countries). Map the whole team across borders.

exercises.title: Caregiver + Backup Person
exercises.blurb: Clear names for who provides daily care and who makes decisions — often different people.

exercises.title: Circle of Influence
exercises.blurb: "Everything is impossible" becomes "here are three things we can do this week."

exercises.title: Relationship Circle
exercises.blurb: A visual map of your whole care team — who is close, who is far, where the gaps are.

name: Voice
tagline: Now your loved one's voice can travel without them.
gain: Care preferences documented, the care recipient's voice made portable — able to travel to hospitals, across borders, into rooms where they cannot be present.
description: Working / Not Working assessment, Decision Making Agreement, Communication Chart. Where the Conspiracy of Silence first gets broken — together.

exercises.title: Working / Not Working
exercises.blurb: An honest assessment of what's going well and what isn't — from every perspective on the team.

exercises.title: Decision Making Agreement
exercises.blurb: A signed agreement about who decides what — so nobody has to guess during a crisis.

exercises.title: Communication Charts
exercises.blurb: The document that explains what your loved one really means when they say "I'm fine."

name: Readiness
gain: Documents gathered, horizons named, the next medical appointment planned.
description: The most operational stage. Every document, every gap, every action item with an owner and a deadline. Now / Next / Later horizon planning.

exercises.title: Health Documents Inventory
exercises.blurb: Every important document from every country, gathered in one place with a clear gap list.

exercises.title: Now/Next/Later Planner
exercises.blurb: Horizon planning — what we handle now, what is coming next, what is later.

exercises.title: Clinic Visit Preparation
exercises.blurb: A complete before / during / after plan for your next medical appointment.

name: Advocacy
gain: Scripts and plans for the conversations you have been putting off — opening line through full encounter plan.
description: Stage 6 is a performance stage. First conversation, branching scripts, full advocacy-encounter plan. Asking is planning, not imposing.

exercises.title: First Conversation Guide
exercises.blurb: The opening line for the conversation you've been putting off — customised to your voice.

exercises.title: Branching Script Builder
exercises.blurb: A five-step script for requesting help without shame — because asking is planning, not imposing.

exercises.title: Advocacy Encounter Plan
exercises.blurb: A full practice conversation with decision branches — if they say yes, if they say no, if they change the subject.

name: Resilience
tagline: You know you can keep doing this.
gain: Burnout caught early, growth named, the team reviewing how care is going.
description: Sustaining what you've built. Burnout Early Warning, Reflective Bookend (which auto-populates from Stage 1's Hopes and Fears), Person-Centred Reviews.

exercises.title: Burnout Early Warning
exercises.blurb: An honest check-in with yourself. Indicator checklist + severity scale + one thing for yourself this week.

exercises.title: Reflective Bookend
exercises.blurb: Your original Hopes and Fears placed next to what actually happened. Name your growth. Leave a message for the next family.

exercises.title: Person-Centred Reviews
exercises.blurb: The full team review — everyone together, looking back at what you have built and planning what comes next.
